sammendrag: In 2004 Germany announced an unemployment insurance (UI) reform that involved reductions to the maximum period over which workers could collect UI benefits. The reductions varied by age and were quite substantial; workers in their 50s and above stood to lose up to 14 months of benefits. The effects of this reform differed dramatically by age and time period. Just before the announced reforms took effect, older workers left their jobs to take up UI at rates roughly five times greater than their pre-announcement levels. After the reforms were in place, older workers reduced their exit rates. Prime-age workers hardly responded at all. We show that these heterogeneous responses are consistent with a simple model that views UI as a precursor to retirement rather than as insurance against unemployment. We estimate that the reform saved Germany roughly 5 billion Euros through the end of 2007, although roughly 20 percent of the savings that are attributable to behavioral responses to the reform were offset by higher costs due to the spike in anticipatory exit rates.
tittel: Unemployment Insurance and Departures from Employment: Evidence from a German Reform
